items.text: Explanation I: - For the purpose of this Section, the expression "agricultural operation" shall mean tilling, sowing, harvesting, crushing of agricultural produce or any other similar operation carried out for the purpose of agriculture; but shall not include the transporting of persons, manure of materials for the purpose of agriculture or the transporting of agricultural produce except when such transporting is made by the owner or occupier of the land for his own purposes, - » Within a distance of fifteen miles from the limits of such land, or (ii) To or from the nearest market place irrespective of the distance of such market from the limits of such land. Explanation II: - For the purpose of this Section, "personal cultivation" means by a person of his own land and on his own account,- (1) by his own labour; (2) by the labour of any member of his family; or (3) by servants on wages payable in cash or kind or both by hired labour under his personal supervision or under the personal supervision of any of his relatives. Repeal and savings of Ordinance No 1 of 2026. 5th MARCH, 2026] ANDHRA PRADESH GAZETTE EXTRAORDINARY 3 STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS Road safety has emerged as a critical public policy priority. A large number of road accidents, fatalities and injuries occurring in the State are attributable to engineering deficiencies, inadequate enforcement, poor road geometries, and lack of protective structures, insufficient road markings and signage, and absence of systematic road safety interventions. To address these issues in a sustained manner, there is an urgent need for dedicated financial resources for continuous road maintenance, corrective engineering, black spot improvement and road safety infrastructure. The reduction of GST on motor vehicles by the Government of India from 28% to 18% has resulted in considerable reduction in the vehicle cost payable by buyers. Hence, levying a nominal cess will not impose any significant financial burden on vehicle owners.

items.text: The reduction of GST on motor vehicles by the Government of India from 28% to 18% has resulted in considerable reduction in the vehicle cost payable by buyers. Hence, levying a nominal cess will not impose any significant financial burden on vehicle owners. The Government has decided to introduce an additional Tax called as “Road Safety Cess” inserting new Section as Section 3-C in the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963 and as per the rates prescribed as per the Tenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963 for utilising the amount for various road safety measures. The “Road Safety Cess” shall be levied and collected on the motor vehicles liable to pay life tax at the time of registration. Accordingly, Government have decided to amend the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963, suitably. As the Legislature was not then in session, having been prorogued and it was decided to give effect to the above decision immediately, the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026 4 ANDHRA PRADESH GAZETTE EXTRAORDINARY [PART IV-A MANDIPALLI RAMPRASAD REDDY MINISTER FOR TRANSPORT, YOUTH & SPORTS (Ordinance No.l of 2026) was promulgated by the Governor on the 12th January, 2026. Introduction of “Road Safety Cess” at the rate of 10% of Life Tax on motor vehicles which are liable to pay life tax duly amending the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963 by inserting a new Section 3-C and by adding the Tenth Schedule after the Ninth Schedule in AP MVT Act 1963; 2. To utilize the money exclusively for improvement of Roads, to undertake critical road safety interventions and reduce road accidents and fatalities. 3. Fiscal Impact and Revenue Realisation is as follows: a. The State registers approximately 73,000 new vehicles per month and 8.7 lakhs new vehicles per year on which life tax is paid. b. With the levy of 10% Road Safety Cess, the anticipated revenue is: i. Monthly Realisation: Rs.22.5 Crores ii. Annual Realisation: Rs. 270 Crores 4. There will not be any burden on the exchequer of the Government due to the above amendments in Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963. Repeal of Ordinance No.4 of 2025. 19th SEPTEMBER, 2025] ANDHRA PRADESH GAZETTE EXTRAORDINARY 3 STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS The Government has enacted the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2006 (Act 33 of 2006) to levy “Green Tax” by inserting a new Section 3-B w.e.f.25-05-2006. According to Section 3-B, an additional tax called as “Green Tax” shall be levied on old motor vehicles suitable for use on road for the purpose of implementation of various measures to control air pollution. The Green Tax is levied in addition to the tax payable under Section 3 of the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963. The maximum rates of Green Tax is leviable as per the rates prescribed in the Fifth Schedule which were fixed in the year 2006. The Government has amended the Fifth Schedule vide Act No.18 of 2021 dated 20-12-2021 (w.e.f. 01-01-2022) fixing the rates of Green Tax to be levied on the old / in-use vehicles basing on the quarterly tax payable by these vehicles. Now, the Government after careful examination of the issue, decided to reduce the rate of “Green tax” and amend the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963, suitably. This Bill seeks to achieve the above decision. MANDIPALLI RAMPRASAD REDDY Minister for Transport, Youth & Sports.

items.text: The Taxes and Fees so collected against Motor Vehicles will help the Government in improving the Road infrastructure, Road Safety and safe and speedy public transport and goods transport. The tax on Motor Vehicles is collected under the provisions of the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963.. Various Schedules under the Act specify tax to be collected against different categories of vehicles originally registered in our State or entering into our State from other States. As on 31-03-2020 there are 1.31 crores Motor Vehicles in the State of Andhra Pradesh. Out of these, 16.24 lakhs are transport vehicles and 1.15 crores are non- transport vehicles. In the category of non-transport vehicles 1.02 crores are 2 wheelers and 8.38 lakhs are 4 wheelers like Motor cars, Jeeps. . Life Tax is collected on all non-transport vehicles which include 2- wheelers / 3-wheelers /4 wheelers used for personal purpose. Life Tax is also levied on some categories of Transport vehicles like Motor cabs, Taxicab etc. The last revision of Life tax was done in the year 2010. Keeping in view the growing inflation and also the increasing in need to improve Road infrastructure, Road Safety and anti pollution measures it is proposed to rationalise the rates of Life Tax. It is ensured that the lower or entry level owners of 2-wheelers and 4-wheeler are not adversely effected. Old and in-use vehicles are > found to be more polluting than the new vehicles .

Hence an additional tax in the name of Green Tax was introduced in respect of old vehicles(over 7 years in case of transport vehicles and over 15 years in case of non-transport vehicles) to act as. disincentive to their continued usage and for the purpose of implementation of various anti pollution measures. There are 4.17 lakhs transport vehicles over 7 years (excluding Autorickshaws and 3- Wheeled Goods Carriages below 3000 kgs in laden weight) and 20.31 lakhs non-transport vehicles over 15 years as on date in the State. Green Tax is collected only when the owner approaches for any transaction in RTA Office. During the financial year 2019-20, Rs. 4.08 | " crores was collected against 1. [unclear figure] lakh transport vehicles and Rs. 0.77 crores was collected against 0.17 lakh non-transport vehicles. The rates of Green Tax were also rationalised keeping in view the need to discourage _ _ older vehicles from plying on the Roads. The last revision of Green tax was done in the year 2006. Accordingly, it has been decided to amend the Andhra క Motor Vehicles Taxation _ Act, 1963 suitably. items.text: 11 శాతం మించనివి . (12) 12 సంవత్సరాలకు మించినవి oe [unclear figure] శాతం ఏడవ అనుసూచిని 7... ప్రధాన చట్టపు ఏడవ అనుసూచిని వదలివేయవలెను. వదిలివేయుట. ANDHRA PRADESH GAZETTE EXTRAORDINARY [PART IV-A ఉద్దేశాలు - కారణాలు మోటారు వాహనాలపై పన్ను ప్రభుత్వ ఆదాయ వనరులలో ప్రధానమైనదిగా ఉన్నది. మోటారు వాహనాలపై ఆ విధంగా వసూలుచేసిన' పన్నులు మరియు ఫీజులు, రహదారుల మౌలిక సదుపాయాలను, రహదారుల భద్రతను మరియు సురక్షితమైన, వేగవంతమైన ప్రజారవాణా మరియు సరకుల రవాణాను మెరుగుపరచుటలో ప్రభుత్వానికి సహాయ పడుతుంది. ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌ మోటారు వాహనముల పన్ను చట్టము, [unclear figure]లోని నిబంధనల క్రింద మోటారు వాహనముల పన్నును వసూలుచేయడం జరుగుతుంది. మన రాష్ట్రంలో మొదటిగా రిజిష్టరు చేయబడిన లేదా ఇతర రాష్ట్రములనుండి మన రాష్ట్రములోకి ప్రవేశించు వివిధ కేటగిరీల వాహనములపై వసూలు చేయవలసిన ' పన్నును ఈ చట్టము God వివిధ షెడ్యూళ్ల నిర్దిష్టరచఢం జరుగుతుంది. [unclear figure] తేదీనాటికి ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌ రాష్ట్రంలో 1.31 కోట్ల మోటారు వాహనాలు ఉన్నాయి. వీటిలో 16.24 లక్షలు రవాణా వాహనాలు కాగా 1.15 కోట్లు రవాణాయేతర వాహనాలు ఉన్నాయి. రవాణాయేతర కేటగిరీలో 1.02 కోట్ల ద్విచక్ర వాహనాలు మరియు [unclear figure] లక్షల మోటారుకార్హు, జీపుల వంటి 4 చక్రాల వాహనాలు ఉన్నాయి. రవాణాయేతర వాహనాలన్నింటిపై జీవితకాల పన్నును వసూలు చేయడం జరుగుతున్నది. ఇందులో వ్యక్తిగత ప్రయోజనాలకు ఉపయోగించే ద్విచక్ర వాహనాలు/త్రిచక్ర వాహనాలు/నాలుగు చక్రాల వాహనాలు ఉన్నాయి, మోటారు క్యాబ్‌లు, ట్యాక్సీ క్యాబ్‌లు మొదలైన కొన్ని కేటగిరీల రవాణా వాహనాలపై కూడా జీవితకాల పన్నును విధించడం జరుగుతుంది. 2010 సంవత్సరములో = జీవితకాల పన్నును చివరిగా సవరించడం జరిగింది. పెరుగుతున్న ద్రవ్యోల్బణాన్ని దృష్టిలో ఉంచుకొని మరియు రహదారుల మౌలిక సదుపాయాలు, రహదారి భద్రత మరియు sreniy నియంత్రణ చర్యలను మెరుగుపరచే అవసరం పెరుగుతున్న దృష్టా జీవితకాల పన్నురేట్లను హేతుబద్ధం చేయాలని (ప్రతిపాదించడం జరిగింది. దీని కారణంగా క్రిందిస్థాయి లేదా ప్రవేశస్థాయి ద్విచక్ర వాహనముల మరియు నాలుగు చక్రముల వాహనముల యజమానులు (ప్రతికూల ప్రభావానికి లోనుకాకుండా చూడటం జరిగింది. SS వాహనముల కంటే పాత మరియు వినియోగములో ఉన్న వాహనములు ఎక్కువ కాలుష్యాన్ని కలిగిస్తున్నట్లుగా కనుగొనడమైనది. అందుచేత, పాత వాహనముల (రవాణా వాహనముల విషయములో 7 సంవత్సరముల పైబడినట్టి మరియు రవాణాయేతర వాహనముల విషయములో 15 నంవత్సరములకు పైబడినట్టి) విషయములో వాటి వినియోగాన్ని కొనసాగిస్తున్నందుకు వారిని నిరుత్సాహపరచే చర్యగా మరియు వివిధ కాలుష్య నిరోధక చర్యలను అమలుపరచునిమిత్తం 'గ్రీన్‌ట్యాక్స్‌' అనే పేరుతో అదనపు పన్నును ప్రవేశపెట్టడం జరిగింది.

items.text: SS వాహనముల కంటే పాత మరియు వినియోగములో ఉన్న వాహనములు ఎక్కువ కాలుష్యాన్ని కలిగిస్తున్నట్లుగా కనుగొనడమైనది. అందుచేత, పాత వాహనముల (రవాణా వాహనముల విషయములో 7 సంవత్సరముల పైబడినట్టి మరియు రవాణాయేతర వాహనముల విషయములో 15 నంవత్సరములకు పైబడినట్టి) విషయములో వాటి వినియోగాన్ని కొనసాగిస్తున్నందుకు వారిని నిరుత్సాహపరచే చర్యగా మరియు వివిధ కాలుష్య నిరోధక చర్యలను అమలుపరచునిమిత్తం 'గ్రీన్‌ట్యాక్స్‌' అనే పేరుతో అదనపు పన్నును ప్రవేశపెట్టడం జరిగింది. 23 NOVEMBER, 2021] ANDHRA PRADESH GAZETTE EXTRAORDINARY రాష్ట్రంలో ఇప్పటి వరకు 7 సంవత్సరముల పైబడిన 4.17 లక్షల రవాణా వాహనములు ([unclear figure] కేజీల రవాణా బరువుకు Sys ఉన్న ఆటోరిక్షాలు మరియు 3 చక్రముల రవాణా వాహనముల మినహా) మరియు 15 సంవత్సరములు పైబడిన 20.31 లక్షల రవాజాయేతర వాహనములు ఉన్నాయి. ఆర్‌.టి.ఏ కార్యాలయంలో ఏదైనా కార్యవ్యవహారమునకు వచ్చినపుడు మాత్రమే యజమాని నుండి గ్రీన్‌ట్యాక్స్‌ వసూలు చేయడం జరుగుతుంది. 2019-20 ఆర్థిక సంవత్సరములో 1.78 లక్షల రవాణా వాహనములపై రూ.ఓ[unclear figure] కోట్లను వసూలు చేయడం జరిగింది. మరియు 0.17 లక్షల రవాణాయేతర వాహనములపై రూ.0.77 కోట్లను వసూలుచేయడం జరిగింది. రహదారులపై రాకపోకల నుండి పాత వాహనములను నిరుత్సాహపరచవలసిన అవసరం ఉన్న దృష్టా గ్రీన్‌ట్యాక్స్‌ రేట్లను కూడా హేతుబద్ధం చేయడం జరిగింది.

items.text: 2019-20 ఆర్థిక సంవత్సరములో 1.78 లక్షల రవాణా వాహనములపై రూ.ఓ[unclear figure] కోట్లను వసూలు చేయడం జరిగింది. మరియు 0.17 లక్షల రవాణాయేతర వాహనములపై రూ.0.77 కోట్లను వసూలుచేయడం జరిగింది. రహదారులపై రాకపోకల నుండి పాత వాహనములను నిరుత్సాహపరచవలసిన అవసరం ఉన్న దృష్టా గ్రీన్‌ట్యాక్స్‌ రేట్లను కూడా హేతుబద్ధం చేయడం జరిగింది. 2006 సంవత్సరములో గ్రీన్‌ట్యాక్స్‌ చివరిసారిగా సవరించడం జరిగింది. . ఆ ప్రకారంగా, ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌ మోటారు వాహనముల పన్ను చట్టము, 1968ను తగిన విధముగా సవరించవలెనని నిర్ణయించడమైనది. ఎయు నిర్ణయాన్ని అమలుపరచుటకు ఈ బిల్లు ఉద్దేశిస్తుంది. పేర్ని వెంకట్రామయ్య (నాని), మరియు ప్రజాసంబంధాల శాఖ మంత్రి, 20 ANDHRA PRADESH GAZETTE EXTRAORDINARY / [PART IV-A ఆర్థిక వివరణ ప్రతిపాదనలలో చేరివున్నవి : i. ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌ మోటారు వాహనముల పన్ను విధింపు చట్టము, 1968లోని మూడవ అనుసూచిలో విహితపరచబడిన మోటారు సైకిల్స్‌ (ద్విదక్రవాహనాలు)పై ఏక మొత్తము/ . జీవితకాలపు పన్ను రేటును పెంచే సబంధన. ii. iii. vi. vii. పరిచ్చేదము [unclear figure]°, ఉప-పరిచ్చేదము (2)లోని రెండో వినాయింపులో కొన్ని పదములను తొలగించడం ద్వారా, ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌ మోటారు వాహనముల పన్ను విధింపు చట్టము, 1963కి కొన్ని సవరణలు చేయు నిబంధన. పరిచ్ళేదము 3లో, ఉప-పరిచ్చేదము (2)లోని ఐదవ వినాయింపును వదలివేయడం ద్వారా, ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌ మోటారు వాహనముల నభ చట్టము, 19638 కొన్ని. సవరణలు చేయు నిబంధన. iv. పరిచ్ళేదము 3-బీలో కొన్ని పదాలను మార్చిడి చేయడం చ్వారా, ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌ మోటారు వాహనముల పన్ను విధింపు చట్టము, 1963కి కొన్ని సవరణలు చేయు నిబంధన. . ANDHRA PRADESH GAZETTE EXTRAORDINARY ~ [PART IV-A ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌ శాసనసభ కార్యకలాప ప్రక్రియ క్రియ మరియు నిర్వహణ నియమావళిలోని 95వ నియమము క్రింద వివరణ. ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్‌ మోటారు వాహనముల పన్ను విధింపు (సవరణ) బిల్లు, 2021ను రాష్ట్ర శాసనమండలి ఆమోదించిన పిమ్మట భారత సంవిధానములోని 200వ అనుచ్చేదము క్రింద అనుమతి నిమిత్తము గవర్నరుకు సమర్పించవలెను, పేర్ని వెంకట్రామయ్య (నాని), మరియు ప్రజాసంబంధాల శాఖ మంత్రి. . వి. బాలకృష్ణమాచార్ములు, | రాష్ట్ర శానన మండలి కార్యదర్శి. [Price : Rs.1-00  RIGHT TO INFORMATION THE ANDHRA PRADESH GAZETTE PART IV-B EXTRAORDINARY PUBLISHED BY AUTHORITY No. 1] AMARA V ATI, TUESDAY, 13th JANUARY, 2026. [1] ANDHRA PRADESH ACTS, ORDINANCES AND REGULATIONS Etc., The following is the authoritative text in English Language of the Ordinance promulgated by the Governor on the 12th January, 2026 is being published under Article 348(3) of the Constitution of India for general information:- ANDHRA PRADESH ORDINANCE No. 1 OF 2026. Promulgated by the Governor in the Seventy-sixth year of the Republic of India. AN ORDINANCE FURTHER TO AMEND THE ANDHRA PRADESH MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION ACT,1963. Whereas, road safety has emerged as a critical public policy priority. A large number of road accidents, fatalities and injuries occurring in the State are attributable to engineering deficiencies, inadequate enforcement, poor road geometries, and lack of protective structures, insufficient road markings and signage, and absence of systematic road safety interventions; And Whereas, to address these issues in a sustained manner, there is an urgent need for dedicated financial resources for continuous road maintenance, corrective engineering, black spot improvement and road safety infrastructure; And Whereas, the reduction of GST on motor vehicles by the Government of India from 28% to 18% has resulted in considerable reduction in the vehicle cost payable by buyers. Hence, levying a nominal cess will not impose any significant financial burden on vehicle owners;

items.text: And Whereas, the reduction of GST on motor vehicles by the Government of India from 28% to 18% has resulted in considerable reduction in the vehicle cost payable by buyers. Hence, levying a nominal cess will not impose any significant financial burden on vehicle owners; J/No - 4/131 2 ANDHRA PRADESH GAZETTE EXTRAORDINARY [PART - IV-B And Whereas, the Government has decided to introduce an additional Tax called as “Road Safety Cess” inserting new section as section 3-C in the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963 and as per the rates prescribed as per the Tenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963 for utilising the amount for various road safety measures. The “Road Safety Cess” shall be levied and collected on the motor vehicles liable to pay life tax at the time of registration; And whereas, Government have decided to amend the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act,1963, suitably; And whereas, the Legislature of the State is not now in session and the Governor of Andhra Pradesh is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action. Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 213 of the Constitution of India, the Governor hereby promulgates the following Ordinance: - 1. (1) This Ordinance may be called the Andhra Pradesh Motor vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance.2026. (2) It shall be come into force at once. 2.

items.text: (1) This Ordinance may be called the Andhra Pradesh Motor vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance.2026. (2) It shall be come into force at once. 2. In the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963 (hereinafter referred to as the Principal Act), after section 3-B, the following new section shall be inserted, namely, - “3-C Levy of Road Safety Cess - There shall be levied and collected an additional tax called “Road Safety Cess” by the Licensing Authority, at the time of registration of motor vehicles liable to pay life tax, at the rates specified in the Tenth Schedule for the purpose of implementation of road safety measures.”. 3. in the Principal Act, after the Ninth Schedule, the following new Schedule shall be inserted, namely, - Short title and commencement. Insertion of new Section 3-C. Act No. 5 of 1963. Insertion of new Schedule - T enth Schedule. 13th January, 2026] ANDHRA PRADESH GAZETTE EXTRAORDINARY 3 S. ABDUL NAZEER, Governor of Andhra Pradesh. items.text: 1 GOVERNMENT OF ANDHRA PRADESH A B S T R A C T Consumer Affairs Food & Civil Supplies Department - Conversion of 5 Kg LPG Tribal Package Cylinders to 14.2 Kg Domestic LPG Cylinders under Deepam-2 Scheme – Orders - Issued. ================================================== CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & CIVIL SUPPLIES (CS-I) DEPARTMENT G.O.MS.No. 22 Dated: 08-09-2025 Read the following:- 1. G.O.Ms.No.12, CA, F & CS (CS-I) Dept., Dated 25.10.2024. 2. From the Commissioner of Civil Supplies, A.P., Vijayawada E file No. FCS02-E/32/2025-PP, Dated:20.08.2025. *** O R D E R :- The Government of Andhra Pradesh, with the objective of achieving 100% LPG coverage and declaring the State as a kerosene-free and eco-friendly cooking fuel State by June 2017, introduced 5 kg LPG cylinder connections for tribal families. Recognizing the difficulties faced by households in hilly and remote tribal areas in transporting and affording the regular 14.2 kg cylinders, the Government decided to supply smaller 5 kg refills, which are easier to carry and cost around Rs.330/- per refill, making them more affordable and convenient. 2. In the G.O.

items.text: 2. In the G.O. 1 st read above, the Government has initiated 3 Free LPG cylinders per year under Deepam-2 scheme from November, 2024 and completed 2 round of supply of free LPG cylinders by 31 st July,2025. More than 1 crore beneficiaries have availed LPG Cylinder refill subsidy to the tune of more than Rs.1500 crore in these two rounds. 3. In the reference 2 nd cited, it is communicated by the Commissioner of Civil Supplies, A.P., Vijayawada that 23,912 LPG consumers having 5 kg connections are covered under the Deepam-2 Scheme. 4. To ensure coverage of all Tribal Area beneficiaries under the Deepam-2 Scheme, the Commissioner of Civil Supplies, A.P., Vijayawada has requested the orders on conversion of cylinders accordingly from 5 kg to 14.2 kg connections. 5. Government after careful examination hereby approve the proposal of the Commissioner of Civil Supplies, A.P., Vijayawada as follows: i. To provide 14.2 Kg domestic LPG connections to 23,912 eligible 5 Kg LPG connections to enable them to get benefits on par with 14.2 Kg connections under the Deepam-2 Scheme. ii. Sanction of necessary budget provision of Rs.5,54,28,016 (Rupees Five Crore Fifty-Four Lakh Twenty-Eight Thousand and Sixteen Only) for security deposit, and documentation charges for 23,912 connections. 2 iii.

items.text: Sanction of necessary budget provision of Rs.5,54,28,016 (Rupees Five Crore Fifty-Four Lakh Twenty-Eight Thousand and Sixteen Only) for security deposit, and documentation charges for 23,912 connections. 2 iii. SF/SC. // FORWARDED :: BY ORDER // SECTION OFFICER ANNEXURE (To G.O.Ms.No.23 , Revenue(Lands-I) Department, dated: 27 .01.2025) Guidelines for distribution of house site pattas under the flagship programme "Housing for All". 1. OBJECTIVE: To provide House Site Pattas to the Homeless Poor People in Rural/ Urban areas in order to facilitate the construction of a Pucca House under the flagship programme “HOUSING FOR ALL”. 2. SIZE/EXTENT OF HOUSE SITE PATTA: A) Rural Area: i. One House Site Patta shall be issued for an extent of 3 Cents to an eligible household in the name of woman beneficiary of the house. ii.

items.text: 2. SIZE/EXTENT OF HOUSE SITE PATTA: A) Rural Area: i. One House Site Patta shall be issued for an extent of 3 Cents to an eligible household in the name of woman beneficiary of the house. ii. The Housing Department shall issue sanction for construction of Individual Housing Unit to the eligible beneficiary under the available schemes. B) Urban Area: i. House Site Patta shall be issued for an extent of 2 Cents as individualplot wherever Government land is available to an eligible beneficiary in the name of the woman of the house. ii. In case of Urban areas wherever Government land is not available, and wherever lands are acquired, housing units will be constructed and handed over to the beneficiaries by APTIDCO/ULB/other Government agency under the available schemes. 3. The State shall execute a conveyance deed for the house site conveying the approval of freehold rights in future (effective from the date of completion of 10 years from the date of assignment) subject to the compliance of Sec-3 of A.P. Assigned lands (POT) Act,1977 (Amendment Act No. 6 of 2024). 4. The eligible beneficiary shall be given House site only once in a lifetime. 5. House shall be constructed by the beneficiary within two years from the date of grant of house site patta/execution of conveyance deed/ sanction of house whichever is later. 6. Plots shall be linked with Aadhar/Ration card so as to avoid duplication of beneficiaries and the data base shall be maintained for future purposes also. 7. ELIGIBILITY:

items.text: 6. Plots shall be linked with Aadhar/Ration card so as to avoid duplication of beneficiaries and the data base shall be maintained for future purposes also. 7. ELIGIBILITY: The following eligibility conditions are to be strictly adhered to for identification of eligible beneficiaries in Rural and Urban Areas. i. The beneficiary shall belong to the identified Below Poverty Line (BPL) category household having white ration card. ii. The beneficiary shall not have an own House/House Site anywhere in the State of Andhra Pradesh. iii. The beneficiary shall not be eligible for issue of house site patta, if he/she has been sanctioned or issued house site patta earlier under any of the schemes of the State Government or Government of India. iv. The Beneficiary shall not have been covered in any previous Housing Scheme of the State/Central Government. v. Households having agricultural land not exceeding Ac.5.00 cts dry or Ac.2.50 cts wet or total land both dry and wet together not exceeding Ac.5.00 cts are eligible. vi. The beneficiary shall possess a valid Aadhaar Card. Aadhaar details shall be collected only with the consent of beneficiary. vii. In case, earlier a house site was allotted to the beneficiary, but possession was not shown due to court cases amount not paid for LA, new house site for 3 / 2 cents in Rural/Urban areas may be allotted duly cancelling the earlier allotment of House Site patta. viii.
items.source: Andhra Pradesh G.O.MS-23 dated 27/01/2025: Lands– Guidelines for distribution of house site pattas under the flagship programme "Housing for All" @ 3 cents in Rural areas and @ 2 cents in Urban areas - Orders-Issu [Revenue department, 2025-01-27]

items.text: In case, earlier house site allotted but beneficiary not willing to construct the house, as it is far away from the habitation/nearby Burial grounds/ Low laying areas/given in another village etc., in entire layout and the earlier allotment may be cancelled and new house site for 3 / 2 cents in Rural/ Urban may be allotted afresh to the beneficiary in the same village or suitable lands. ix. In cases, wherein the beneficiaries have not constructed houses in part of the layout, earlier house site patta may be cancelled and new house site patta for 3 / 2 cents in Rural/ Urban may be allotted afresh to the beneficiary x. In cases of random plots which are vacant in a layout or in cases of resumption the earlier allotment shall be cancelled and may be allotted to a willing eligible beneficiary for 1.5 cents in rural and 1 cent in urban. 8. METHOD OF SELECTION: a. The Applications shall be invited at Village/Ward Level considering village/town as a unit respectively. b. All applications shall be enquired by the VRO/RI for adherence to the eligibility conditions, as prescribed. c. The draft List of identified eligible beneficiaries shall be published at Village/Ward Secretariat calling for further claims & objections. d. Grama/Ward Sabha shall be conducted to finalise the list of beneficiaries duly redressing the claims & objections, e. The final list of beneficiaries shall be submitted for approval of the District Collector by the Tahsildars and Municipal Commissioners in the Rural and Urban areas respectively. f.

items.text: The final list of beneficiaries shall be submitted for approval of the District Collector by the Tahsildars and Municipal Commissioners in the Rural and Urban areas respectively. f. The final list of beneficiaries approved by the District Collector shall be published in the respective Village/Ward Secretariat. g. In case of any further claims or objections, the Tahsildar/Municipal Commissioner shall function as the redressal officer duly taking approval from the District Collector. h. In case suitable land is not available in the village for the grant of House site pattas, but is available in neighbouring village/villages, the District Collector may as a special case, permit the same. 9. IDENTIFICATION OF LANDS: The District Collectors shall identify: a. All available Government lands, b. Lands under the possession of Government institutions/ corporations and other Government bodies which are far beyond their requirement, considering that the said lands are suitable for providing house sites shall be resumed as per procedure, c. Lands available in the industrial parks developed by APIIC which are suitable for House sites/ Housing Units shall be utilised for industrial labour, d. Lands that can be made available under land pooling scheme, e. Eligible Beneficiaries possessing Own Sites in Gramakantam shall be identified for construction of Houses by issuing possession certificates. f. House sites issued previously by various departments that remain unutilized and kept vacant without construction of houses shall be identified for this purpose and resumed following due procedure. g. The District Collectors shall identify landowners who are willing to donate their lands for this noble cause i.e, housing programme for needy homeless people in the society. h.

items.text: The District Collectors shall identify landowners who are willing to donate their lands for this noble cause i.e, housing programme for needy homeless people in the society. h. The District Collectors are instructed to take up land acquisition either by purchase through negotiation or through compulsory acquisition as a last resort only after exhausting all other possibilities. i. The Assigned lands shall be resumed for this purpose only in rare cases when no other alternative land is available. The compensation shall be paid as per existing guidelines. 10. The Village or Town shall be taken as a Unit for identification of suitable lands for providing house sites. 11. The District Collectors shall handover the identified Government Lands to the Housing/MA&UD Departments in the Rural/ Urban areas respectively. 12. Housing/MA&UD Departments shall prepare layouts as per norms in the identified Government Lands handed over by the Revenue Department, so as to avoid delay for distribution of House Site Pattas. The Village/Town shall be maintained as a unit. 13. The Department of Survey and Land Records shall assist in identification of land, Survey, Sub-division, preparation of layouts and peg-marking. 14. RELEASE OF FUNDS: Budgetary support shall be provided by the Revenue Department to the District Collectors for the following activities: a. Payment of compensation for land acquisition. b. Preparation of layouts & plotting of individual sites. c. Other contingencies arising for implementation of the program. 15. CANCELLATION: a. The allotment of House Site Patta will be cancelled immediately in case, if it is established that the same has been obtained by fraud or suppression of facts. The cancelled House Site Patta will be allotted to other eligible beneficiary. b.

items.text: 15. CANCELLATION: a. The allotment of House Site Patta will be cancelled immediately in case, if it is established that the same has been obtained by fraud or suppression of facts. The cancelled House Site Patta will be allotted to other eligible beneficiary. b. In the reference second read above, the Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps, Andhra Pradesh, issued certain instructions relating to the levy of stamp duty and registration fee on partition deeds executed among family members. However, these instructions have led to many audit objections and numerous representations from the registering public, stating that the instructions are not in accordance with the provisions of the Indian Stamp Act,1899 and are causing undue hardship. Therefore, the Commissioner and Inspector General, Registration and Stamps, Andhra Pradesh, in the reference 4th read above, has requested the Government to revise the existing instructions and enforce a uniform procedure for the levy of stamp duty on partition deeds. 3. items.text: 3. In the reference 5 th read above, the Commissioner and Inspector General of Registration and Stamps, Andhra Pradesh further informed that a substantial portion of partitions take place without registration, particularly during succession-based mutations, which bypass the revenue-generating framework. In the event of intestate death (i.e., without a will), the legal heirs acquire property as co-parceners with undivided shares, as per personal succession laws (e.g., Hindu Succession Act, 1956). Mutation is often done based on legal heir certificates or affidavits, without insisting on a registered partition deed, in violation of Section 17(1)(b) of the Registration Act, 1908, which mandates registration of non- testamentary instruments affecting immovable property. In view of this, the Commissioner and Inspector General has requested the Government to modify the orders issued in the G.O first cited and to prescribe slab-wise fixed stamp duty under Article 40 of Schedule 1-A of Indian Stamp Act, 1899 be adopted specifically for ancestral agricultural property partitions devolved by succession in cases of intestate deaths in addition to the existing provisions. 4. Government after careful examination of the matter hereby insert a provision in respect of article 40 of Schedule 1A to Indian Stamp Act, 1899 amending the notification issued in G.O.Ms.No.395, Revenue (Regn.1) Department, dated 26.11.2014, prescribing stamp duty on partition deeds executed in respect of ancestral agricultural properties devolving by succession in cases of intestate deaths.

items.text: He has further reported that, as per Section 91 of AP Municipalities Act, 1965 and Section 269 (2) of Municipal Corporation Act, 1955 – “a simple interest at the rate of two percent (2%) per month shall be charged in case of failure to pay property tax by the end of the month of June for the first half year and by the end of the month of December for the second half year.” 2.The C&DMA, AP has also reported that, though the Government had issued orders in G.O.Ms.No.35, dated:29.02.2024 to waive-off the interest accumulated on arrears and current year of property tax i.e., up to the year 2023-24 as one-time measure in all ULBs, provided the assesse pays the total arrears and current year tax in one lump sum on or in installments on or before 31.03.2024 and to adjust the interest already paid by the tax payers on arrears towards the future tax payments, the property tax collections in the financial year 2023-24 was not up to mark as all Municipal Staff were engaged in duties related to Assembly Elections -2024. 3.Further, as per operational guidelines under 15 th Finance Commission, it is mandatory on the part of ULBs to show consistent improvement in the collection of property tax in line with growth rate of State's own GDP from the financial year 2025- 26, to get eligibility for claiming the 15th Finance Grant.

items.text: 4.In the above context, the C&DMA, AP has requested the Government to consider 50% waive-off the interest accumulated on arrears of property tax up to the year 2024-25 as one time measure in all ULBs so as to improve the Collections of ULBs, give benefit of waiver of 50% interest to the taxpayers and to encourage them to settle the long pending dues, critical cases & court cases amicably out of court. (P.T.O) :: 2 :: 5.Government, after careful examination of the matter keeping in view the objective to improve the Collections of ULBs as well as welfare of the assesses and in exercise of the powers conferred under the Section 387-A of the AP Municipalities Act, 1965 under the Section 679-E of Municipal Corporations Act, 1955 hereby order: (i) to waive-off 50% of the interest accumulated on arrears and current year property tax (Buildings and Vacant Lands) dues up to the financial year 2024-25 as one-time measure in all ULB’s, provided the assesse pays the total property tax arrears and current year dues together with 50% interest in one lump sum on or before 31.03.2025 and (ii) to adjust the interest already paid by the Tax payers on arrears and on current year demand during the current financial year i.e., 2024-25 towards the future property tax payments up to the extent 50% of interest paid and no cash refund shall be made, subject to clearance of all dues by 31.03.2025.

L. A. Bill No. 3 of 2026 [1] Short title and commencement. A BILL FURTHER TO AMEND THE ANDHRA PRADESH ELECTRICITY DUTY ACT, 1939. Be it enacted by the Legislature of the State of Andhra Pradesh in the Seventy-Seventh Year of the Republic of India as follows:- 1. (1) This Act may be called the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Duty (Amendment) Act, 2026. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force with effect on and from 26th August, 2021. 2. In the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Duty Act, 1939 (hereinafter referred to as the Principal Act), in section 3,- (i) in sub-section (1), after the words “consumer categories” and before the words “which shall not be”, the following shall be inserted, namely,- Amendment of section 3. (ii) after sub-section (4), the following sub-section shall be added, namely,- “(5) Every licensee is entitled to recover from any person or class of persons to whom energy is sold at more than twelve paisa per unit, the duty which falls to be paid by the licensee in respect of the energy so sold or any part of it, as may be determined by the State Government. Explanation: (a) Save as otherwise provided in sub-section (4) of section 3, the duty recoverable from any person under this section shall not be deemed to be part of the price charged for the energy by the licensee. (b) The licensee may, for the purpose of sub-section (5), exercise the power conferred on a licensee by sub-section (1) of section 56 of the Electricity Act, 2003, for the recovery of any charge or sum due in respect of energy supplied by it.”. 3. Validation:- Notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of any Court or other authority to the contrary, any electricity duty levied, charged or collected or purporting to have been levied, charged or collected before the commencement of this Act and any action taken or thing done before the commencement in relation to such levy or collection under the provisions of the Principal Act shall be deemed to be as valid and effective as if such levy or collection or action or thing had been made, taken or done under the Principal Act as amended by this Act and accordingly- (1) All levy and collection by the licensee in connection with electricity duty for all purposes between 26th August, 2021 and 19th December, 2024 shall be deemed to be and to have always been done or taken in accordance with the law; (2) All Notifications issued by the State Government under the Act between 26th August, 2021 and 19th December, 2024 shall be deemed to have been issued in accordance with the law;

Government. The duty at the rate of 6 paise per unit sale had been levied with effect from 1st December, 1993, by way of the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Duty (Amendment) Act, 1994 (Act No.l of 1994). Since then, the same rate of duty has continued for about 28 years. The Government, considering the substantial gap of 28 years in electricity duty revision, and after duly studying the current rates of levy of duty across other States like Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Himachal Pradesh, Kerala, Manipur, Punjab, West Bengal, and Jammu & Kashmir where the rate of duty varies from 14 paise to 180 paise per unit sale of energy on different categories of consumers, felt it necessary to enhance the duty rates under the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Duty Act, 1939. Further, the term “Licensee” under sub-section (b) of section 2 of the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Duty Act, 1939 was defined in terms of the licensee referable to the Indian Electricity Act, 1910.

items.text: GOVERNMENT OF ANDHRA PRADESH ABSTRACT CA,F&CS Department – Extension of subsidy to Domestic Piped Natural Gas (PNG) Consumers on par with LPG beneficiaries under DEEPAM-2 Scheme – Orders – Issued. ================================================== CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & CIVIL SUPPLIES (CS-I) DEPARTMENT G.O.MS.No. 3 Dated: 10-04-2026 Read the following:- 1. G.O.Ms.12, CA,F & CS Department, Dated 25-10-2024. 2. E file No.3187731 received from Andhra Pradesh Gas Infrastructure Corporation Ltd. ORDER: The Government of Andhra Pradesh has consistently endeavoured to provide citizens with access to clean and affordable cooking fuel. The successful implementation of the DEEPAM-2 scheme, which provides a subsidy on LPG refills, has significantly benefited households across the state. 2. To further this objective and encourage the adoption of a safer, more convenient, and environmentally friendly fuel, this proposal outlines a framework for providing a subsidy to domestic consumers of Piped Natural Gas (PNG). The proposed scheme, titled as the "Andhra Pradesh PNG Subvention Scheme," aims to facilitate the large-scale conversion of households from LPG to PNG. 3. The promotion of Piped Natural Gas is a strategic priority for reducing the logistics burden associated with LPG cylinders.

items.title: Andhra Pradesh G.O.MS-3 dated 10/04/2026: CA,F&CS Department – Extension of subsidy to Domestic Piped Natural Gas (PNG) Consumers on par with LPG beneficiaries under DEEPAM-2 Scheme – Orders – Issued.

items.text: The proposed scheme, titled as the "Andhra Pradesh PNG Subvention Scheme," aims to facilitate the large-scale conversion of households from LPG to PNG. 3. The promotion of Piped Natural Gas is a strategic priority for reducing the logistics burden associated with LPG cylinders. A direct subsidy will provide the necessary impetus for consumers to make the initial switch and will offer them financial relief, mirroring the benefits currently extended to LPG users under the DEEPAM-2 scheme. 4. Government, after careful examination, has observed that Piped Natural Gas (PNG) is a safer, environmentally friendly, and efficient alternative to LPG. However, the absence of subsidy support has limited its adoption among domestic consumers. 5. In line with the policy objective of promoting cleaner fuels and to encourage piped gas usage, Government hereby decides to extend subsidy support to Domestic Piped Natural Gas (PNG) consumers on par with LPG beneficiaries under DEEPAM-2 Scheme and hereby accords sanction for implementation of “Andhra Pradesh PNG Subvention Scheme” with the following provisions: •Subsidy amount: Rs.2,400/- (Rupees Two Thousand Four Hundred Only) per annum per domestic PNG connection. •Applicable only to eligible DEEPAM-2 beneficiaries. (P.T.O) :2: •PNG Subsidy shall be made applicable to the eligible consumers only after they have surrendered the LPG connection that is otherwise eligible for Deepam-2 Scheme subsidy. 6.

items.text: (P.T.O) :2: •PNG Subsidy shall be made applicable to the eligible consumers only after they have surrendered the LPG connection that is otherwise eligible for Deepam-2 Scheme subsidy. 6. Mode of Disbursement: •Subsidy shall be transferred through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). •Annual subsidy shall be disbursed in six instalments aligned with bi- monthly PNG billing cycle. 7. Eligibility Conditions: •Domestic PNG consumer with valid connection from authorized City Gas Distribution (CGD) entity. •Must be an eligible beneficiary under DEEPAM-2 Scheme. •Aadhaar-linked bank account mandatory. •No duplication of benefit (LPG + PNG subsidy shall not be allowed to the same household). 8. Implementation Mechanism: •Civil Supplies Department shall be the nodal agency. •CGD companies shall share verified consumer database. •Aadhaar-based e-KYC and de-duplication shall be carried out to arrive at the eligibility along with other parameters as applicable for Deepam-2 scheme. •A dedicated portal shall be developed for beneficiary management. 9. Role of CGD Entities: CGD companies shall: •Maintain updated consumer database. •Facilitate Aadhaar seeding and e-KYC. •Share billing and payment data. •Assist in beneficiary verification. •Establish grievance redressal systems. 10. Financial Implications: •Expenditure shall be met from the budget allocated for DEEPAM-2. •Budget allocation shall be based on number of PNG consumers and revised periodically. (P.T.O) :3: 11.

Implementation of PNG Scheme and Selection of Beneficiaries:- (i) The City Gas Distribution (CGD) entities sh all collect Aadhaar details of all PNG connection holders, including tenants. items.text: Further, the registration fee to be levied on such cancellation deeds is Rs.1000/- which shall be payable by the person presenting such document for registration as per Table of Fees under G.O.M.S.No.463. Dt:17.08.2013 in addition to user charges of Rs.500/-. 2. The Inspector General, Registration & Stamps, AP has therefore requested the Government to grant exemption of registration fee and user charges on the cancellation deeds executed under the orders of the Competent Authorities under proviso Rule 26(k)(i) of Andhra Pradesh Rules under the Registration Act-1908 as execution of cancellation deeds becomes necessary to nullify the illegal alienation of Government/ Assigned/ Endowment/ Waqf lands prohibited from registration under section 22-A of the Registration Act,1908 and it will aid in promotion of prevention of alienation of Government lands and resumption of such lands in violation of assignment conditions originally assigned to poor families from the marginalised sections of the society. 3. Government after careful examination of the matter, have decided to exempt the Registration Fee and user charges on the cancellation deeds executed by the Revenue/any authorities under the orders of the Competent Authorities under proviso Rule 26(k)(i) of Andhra Pradesh Rules under the Registration Act-1908, as this exemption is for the purpose of nullifying the illegal alienation of Government/ Assigned/ Endowments/Waqf lands prohibited under Sec 22-A of the Registration Act, 1908. Further, between 2019 and 2024, the uncertainty stemming from the announcement of the establishment of three capitals led to consid erable confusion among the institutions allocated land. This ambiguity has resulted in partial constructions, delays in the execution of sale agreements and payments. In order to build confidence and bring anchor investors to start the construction activity at good place in Amaravati, it is required to provide certain exemptions. Provision of stamp duty exemption builds up the credence in the Educational and Healthcare Institutions that have been allotted land in Amaravati. 3. The APCRDA in the reference 1st read above, has informed that the APCRDA in its 48th Authority Meeting held on 2nd June, 2025 passed resolution No.546/2025 that “Educational and Healthcare Institutions which are allotted land in the Capital City, Amaravati, on or after 01.01.2025, shall be exempted from payment of stamp duty on reimbursement basis while executing Agreement of Sale/Lease and Lease/Sale Deed”. The APCRDA has requested the Government to take necessary further action in the matter. 4. Accordingly, the MA&UD Department in the reference 2 nd read above, has furnished the proposals for exemption of stamp duty under Section 9(1)(a) of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 for the lands allotted by the MA&UD (CRDA) Department on or after 01.01.2025 for the following Educational and Healthcare Institutions in the Capital City, Amaravati, on a reimbursement basis while executing Agreements of Sale/Lease and Lease/Sale Deeds” duly placing the matter before the Council of Ministers along with Council resolution:

In the reference 4 th read above, the Inspector General, Registration and Stamps A.P. has stated that out of Ac.2200.00cts, Ac.1035.53cts is patta land and Ac.1164.47cts of land is Govt. land. The MV for Ac.1035.53 cts of patta land as per 3 market value guidelines approved by the committee is Rs.160,42,88,800/-. In terms of G.O.Ms.No.76 of the Industries and Commerce (P&I) Department, the Government decided to allot Ac.2200.00 cents @ Rs.51,39,690/ - per Acre and total value for Ac.2200.00 cents as per allotment price works out to Rs.1130,73,18,000/ -. Since total sale consideration is higher than market value fixed as per MVGR, the financial implications are calculated on sale consideration. As such, total stamp duty including transfer duty and registration fees to be levied on sale agreement followed by sale deed arrived to Rs.84,80,68,850/-.

items.text: GOVERNMENT OF ANDHRA PRADESH ABSTRACT Registration & Stamps – Certain amendments to the Andhra Pradesh Rules under the Registration Act, 1908 - Notification – Orders – Issued. =================================================== REVENUE (REGISTRATION -1) DEPARTMENT G.O.Ms.No.2 Dated: 02-01-2026. Read the following: - 1. G.O.Ms.No.235, Revenue (Regn-I) Department, dt. 9-7-2025. 2. From the Inspector General, Registration & Stamps, AP e-file bearing computer No. 188489, dt. 17-12-2025. ***** O R D E R: In the G.O. first read above, certain amendments were made to The Registration Act, 1908 by Act No. 1 of 2024 “The Registration ( Andhra Pradesh Amendment) Act, 2023”. 2. In the reference 2nd read above, the Inspector General, Registration & Stamps, AP has submitted a draft Registration Rules under Section 69 of the Registration Act, 1908 for issue of Amendment of the Andhra Pradesh Registration Rules, 1908 in accordance with the G.O 1st cited. 3. After careful examination of the matter, Government hereby accepted the proposal of the Inspector General, Registration & Stamps, AP and issued the following amendments to the Andhra Pradesh Rules under the Registration Act, 1908. 4. Accordingly, the following notification will be published in the Andhra Pradesh Gazette.

After careful examination of the matter, Government hereby accepted the proposal of the Inspector General, Registration & Stamps, AP and issued the following amendments to the Andhra Pradesh Rules under the Registration Act, 1908. 4. Accordingly, the following notification will be published in the Andhra Pradesh Gazette. NOTIFICATION In exercise of the powers conferred under Section 69 of The Registration Act, 1908, the Government of Andhra Pradesh hereby makes the following amendments to the Andhra Pradesh Rules under the Registration Act, 1908. AMENDMENT In the said Rules:- In the heading of Chapter VII, after the figures “21,22(i)”, the following shall be inserted, namely: “(22(C))” 2. In Rule 20, after Sub Rule (A), the following Sub Rules shall be inserted namely, 20-B(i): A document or electronic record shall be treated as f orged for the purpose of these Rules if it has been dishonestly or fraudulently made, signed, sealed, executed, transmitted, or altered, in whole or in part, so as to purport that it was made, signed, sealed, executed, transmitted, or altered by or with the authority of a person by whom or by whose authority it was not so made, signed, sealed, executed, transmitted, or altered, with the intention of causing it to be acted upon or accepted as genuine. Provided that the fact of forgery shall be deemed established only upon a finding or declaration to that effect made by a competent Court of law, and such finding or declaration shall be brought to the notice of the Registering Officer before any action is taken under this Rule. (ii):

items.text: Provided that the fact of forgery shall be deemed established only upon a finding or declaration to that effect made by a competent Court of law, and such finding or declaration shall be brought to the notice of the Registering Officer before any action is taken under this Rule. (ii): No document which is forg ed, as defined in sub -rule (i), shall be accepted for registration under the Act, or the Rules made thereunder. Where a competent court has declared a document to be forged, and the same has been brought to the notice of the Registering Officer, such Regis tering Officer shall refuse to register the said document. The Registering Officer shall record the reasons for such refusal in writing in Book No. 2, in accordance with Rule 161 of these Rules.. 20 C (i): No document purporting to transfer, assign, convey, gift, mortgage, lease, exchange or otherwise deal with any immovable property which is under permanent or provisional attachment by a competent authority having statutory competence under any Central Act or State Act for the time being in force, or by o rder of any Court or Tribunal exercising powers conferred by law, shall be registered during the subsistence of such attachment. (ii) Every order of attachment issued by any authority, shall clearly disclose the statutory provision under which such authority is competent to issue the order. The Registering Officer shall verify the disclosure of such statutory competence before acting upon the order. (iii) If the Registering Officer is satisfied that the order of attachment is issued by a competent authority under valid statutory powers, he shall refuse registration of the concerned document under Section 71 of the Act, recording reasons in writing.

items.text: (iii) If the Registering Officer is satisfied that the order of attachment is issued by a competent authority under valid statutory powers, he shall refuse registration of the concerned document under Section 71 of the Act, recording reasons in writing. (iv) Where, upon scrutiny, the Registering Officer finds that an order of attachment does not disclose the statutory competence of the issuing authority, the Registering Officer shall, without delay, notify the issuing authority to disclose the statutory provision under which such order has been issued and shall communicate the same forthwith; and such order shall not be acted upon until the deficiency is rectified. (v).(a) Every officer competent to issue an order of attachment shall set forth therein full particulars of the property, including the name of the District, Mandal, Village, Survey Number / Town Survey Number, Sub-Division, Layout Permit Number, Extent, Door Number and plinth area in the case of a house or building, and the four boundaries thereof an d send it to the Registering Officer, in whose jurisdiction the attached property is situated, along with an intimation in the proforma prescribed in Appendix-XI (b) The Registering Officer shall, on receipt of the attachment order and the intimation thereof, verify and satisfy himself that full particulars of the property are duly furnished and if not so furnished, he shall return the same to the competent authority for retransmission after supplying the omissions. (c) No Registering Officer shall act upon or give effect to any attachment order unless the requirements of clause (a) of this rule are duly complied with. (vi):

(vi): Upon receipt of an order of attachment along with intimation in accordance with sub-rules (ii) to (v), the Registering Officer shall forthwith make an entry in the Prohibited Property Register maintained in his office, specifying the particulars of the property, and the date of receipt of such order. (vii): Where the attachment is vacated, withdrawn, or set aside by the competent authority, Court, or Tribunal, and such order is duly communicated, the Registering Officer shall, after verifying its authenticity, forward the matter to the Registrar of the District for removal of the entry from the Prohibited Property Register. 3) For rule 26 (i) (k), the following, shall be substituted namely,:- 26 (i) (k) (i) The registering officer shall ensure, at the time of presentation for registration of cancellation deeds of previously registered deeds of conveyance on sale before him, that such cancellation deeds are executed by all the executant and claimant parties to the previously registered conveyance on sale and that such cancellation deed is accompanied by a declaration showing mutual consent or an order of a competent Civil or High Court or the State or Central Government annulling the transaction contained in the previously registered deed of conveyance on sale. Provided that notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or these Rules, the Registering Officer shall register documents, cancelling any previously registered document, executed by a Civil Judge or an authority constituted under any statute or the Government competent to execute such deeds.

(ii) Save in the manner provided for above, no cancellation deed of a previously registered deed of conveyance on sale before him shall be accepted for presentation for registration. 4) In Rule 161, after sub -rule (XVI), the following sub -rule shall be inserted, namely: (XVII): Section 22 -C – That the document is found to be in contravention of the provisions of Section 22-C. 5) In the heading of Chapter XXV, the figures “72 to 77 -B” shall be substituted for the figures “72 to 76”. 6) After Rule 181 in Chapter XXV, the following Rules shall be added, namely:- 181-A: (i) The Registrar may, on a complaint received from any person, initiate proceedings for cancellation of the registration of any document under Section 77- A of the Act, where such document is found to have been registered in contravention of the provisions of Section 22-A, Section 22-B, or Section 22-C of the Act.

items.text: (ii)The Registrar may, suomotu, initiate such proceedings based on a. the findings of any inspection or enquiry or verification by the departmental authorities or any audit or; b. information received from the Government authorities, which disclose contravention or violation of the provisions of Section 22-A or Section 22-B or Section 22-C of the Act (iii) Every complaint under sub-rule (i) shall be submitted in writing to the Registrar within whose jurisdiction the document was registered, in the format prescribed in Form–1 of the Appendix–XII, and shall be accompanied by – (a) particulars of the document sought to be cancelled, including its registration number, date of registration and names of the parties thereto; (b) specific allegations of contravention of the provisions of Section 22 -A or Section 22-B or Section 22-C of the Act, supported by documentary evidence such as copies of prior registered documents, affidavits or official records. N.B.—No fee shall be payable for filing a complaint under this sub-rule. (c)Upon receipt of the complaint, the Registrar shall issue an acknowledgment to the complainant in Form–2of the Appendix–XII.

(c)Upon receipt of the complaint, the Registrar shall issue an acknowledgment to the complainant in Form–2of the Appendix–XII. (iv) The Registrar shall conduct a preliminary examination of the complaint or the grounds for suomotu action within fifteen day s from the date of its receipt or ascertainment, as the case may be, and if a prima facie case is made out, shall commence proceedings; or where no such case is made out, reject the complaint or drop the suomotu action, recording reasons therefor in a regi ster to be maintained in Form-3 of the Appendix-XII. 181-B (i) Upon initiation of proceedings under Rule 181-A, the Registrar shall issue a notice in Form -4 of the Appendix -XII, to all parties to the document and to such other persons who, in his opinion, may be affected by the proposed cancellation. (ii) Service of notice under sub-rule (i) shall be effected (a) by registered post with acknowledgment due; or (b) by electronic mail, where the e-mail address is available in the records; or (c) by publication in one local newspaper having circulation in the area, where the address of any persons is unknown or cannot be reasonably ascertained. (iii) Every notice issued under sub-rule (i) shall specify— (a) the particulars of the document pro posed to be cancelled and the alleged contravention; (b) copies of the relevant material, records or evidence relied upon;

items.text: (iii) Every notice issued under sub-rule (i) shall specify— (a) the particulars of the document pro posed to be cancelled and the alleged contravention; (b) copies of the relevant material, records or evidence relied upon; (c) a direction to submit a reply in writing, supported by affidavits and documentary evidence, within fifteen days from the date o f receipt of the notice; and (d) an intimation that, in the event of failure to submit a reply within stipulated time, may result in the proceedings being decided ex parte. (iv) For the purposes of conducting proceedings relating to cancellation of documents registered in contravention of Sections 22-A, 22-B, or 22-C of the Act, the Registrar shall have the power to summon the executants, witnesses or any person concerned, and to enforce their attendance or production of documents in accordance with Section 77 -A of the Act. The Registrar shall conduct the enquiry as summary proceedings, and no such proceedings shall be commenced unless notice has been duly served in the manner specified in sub-rule (ii). (v) Upon conclusion of the enquiry, if the Registrar is satisfied that the document has been registered in contravention of Section 22 -A, Section 22-B or Section 22 - C of the Act, he shall record such finding in writing and proceed further in accordance with the procedure prescribed under these rules.

items.text: (vi) Where the Registrar determines that no contravention of Section 22-A, Section 22-B or Section 22-C of the Act is established, he shall record such finding in writing and pass an order rejecting the complaint, holding that matter does not fall within the ambit of Section 77-A of the Act. 181-C (i) For the purpose of taking a decision on the finding recorded by the Registrar under Rule 181-B (v), a Committee shall be constituted, consisting of— (a) the District Collector as Chairperson; (b) the Joint Collector as Member; (c) the Revenue Divisional Officer concerned as Member; and (d) the Registrar as Convenor. (ii) The committee shall meet, within fifteen days from the date of referral by the Registrar, and (a) review the proposal of the Registrar, the replies received, if any, and the evidence adduced; (b) verify the facts against official records; and (c) The Committee shall record its decision in writing and forward the same to the Registrar. (iii) Upon receipt of the Committee ’s written decision, the Registrar shall, within seven days, pass the final order strictly in accordance with the decision of the Committee, either cancelling the registration of the document or rejecting the proposal, as the case may be, and shall communicate the order to all concerned parties.

items.text: 181-D (i) The Inspector General of Registration shall, on noticing any violation of Sections 22A, 22B or 22C of the Act, in respect of any registered document, either on a complaint of any person or on a reference from any Government authority, issue notices to all parties to the document and such other persons interested therein informing them the violation and asking them to show cause within a stipulated period as to why the said document should not be cancelled in view of the said violation. (ii) he shall, afte r considering the replies received or after expiry of the period stipulated in the notice, take appropriate action either cancelling the registration of the document or rejecting the compliant. 181-E Where cancellation of document is ordered under sub-rule (iii) of Rule 181 C or under Sub Rule (ii) of Rule 181 D— (i) the order of cancellation shall be communicated to the Registering Officer concerned, who shall, mutatis mutandis take further action thereon as per the procedure prescribed in rule 118 of these rules. (ii) intimation of the cancellation shall be sent forthwith to all affected persons and to the concerned Revenue, Municipal and Panchayat authorities, and the respective officers shall carry out the necessary changes in their records in accordance with the order of the Registrar. 181-F. (i) The appeal to be submitted to the Inspector General of Registration shall be in Form-5 of the Appendix XII and be accompanied by a copy of the order appealed against and a copy of the document in question wi thin thirty days from the date of receipt of order issued by the Registrar.

(ii) The Inspector General shall dispose of the appeal within six months from the date of its receipt and communicate his orders to the Registrar concerned, besides appellant. (iii) On the further appeal against the order of the Inspector General of Registration, the committee constituted, consisting of- (a) the Principal Secretary to Government, Revenue (Registration) Department, as Chairperson; (b) the Inspector General of Registration as Member-Secretary; (c) the Secretary to Government, Law Department, or his nominee (iv) The committee shall take a decision on the appeal within six months and within three weeks thereafter, the Government shall issue orders in pursuance of the decision of the Committee. 7) In the heading of Chapter XXVII, the words and figure (“Section 83”) shall be substituted by the following, -namely; (“Sections 81-A, 81-B and 83”) 8) In between the Rules 188 and 189, the following Rules shall be inserted, namely:- 188-A.(i) Where it appears to the Inspector General of Registration or the Registrar that a registering officer or any person employed in his office has registered a document in contravention of the provisions of Section 22 -A or Section 22 -B or Section 22-C of the Act, such officer shall cause an inquiry to be conducted into the matter.

items.text: (ii) The inquiry under sub-rule (i) shall be initiated either suomotu or on receipt of a complaint in writing and shall be conducted in a summary manner by the Registrar. (iii) The complaint referred to in sub-rule (ii) shall be accompanied by— (a) particulars of the document registered in contravention, including its registration number, date of registration and names of the parties thereto; and (b) specific allegations of contravention, supported by evidence such as copies of the document, relevant records or affidavits. (iv) Upon initiation of the inquiry, a show cause notice shall be issued to the registering officer or the person employed, in Form-1 of the Appendix-XIII, to these rules, calling upon him to furnish a reply in writing within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice, explaining why action under Section 81 -A of the Act should not be taken. (v) The Registrar shall, after considering the reply, if a ny, and after affording an opportunity of personal hearing if requested, submit a report to the Inspector General of Registration within three months from the date of initiation of the inquiry, recommending whether the contravention is established or whether the act was done in good faith as defined in the Explanation to sub -section (2) of Section 81-A of the Act.
items.source: Andhra Pradesh G.O.MS-2 dated 02/01/2026: Registration & Stamps – Certain amendments to the Andhra Pradesh Rules under the Registration Act, 1908 - Notification – Orders – Issued. [REV department, 2026-01-02]

items.text: (vi) For the purposes of determining good faith under sub-section (2) of Section 81- A of the Act, the Registrar shall consider— (a) whether the registering officer acted in accordance with the provisions of Act, Rules, departmental guidelines and circulars in registering the document against the provisions of Section 22-A, Section 22-B or Section 22-C ; Provided that, where the Registrar is unable to establish such contravention beyond reasonable doubt in respect of properties covered under Section 22-A, he may seek confirmation from the competent authority which had furnished the particulars of the prohibited property. Provided further that, where any act or omission by a Registering Officer, or by any person presenting or executing a document, amounts to a contravention of the provisions of the Act or these Rules, such act or omission shall not be deemed a willful contravention on the part of the Registering Officer if it is found to have arisen from a bona fide mistake of fact, committed in good faith, and under a belief justified by law, as envisaged under Section 17 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita. For the purposes of this rule, bona fide mistakes may include, but are not limited to, the errors arising from— (a) clerical or typographical mistakes in the preparation or entry of documents; (b) inadvertent misinterpretation of facts presented by the executant or claimant parties; (c) reliance on official records or certificates which are subsequently found to be incorrect or incomplete;

(vii) Where the report under sub-rule (v) establishes that the contravention was not committed in good faith, the Inspector General of Registration shall, after due examination, authorize the Regis trar to initiate prosecution. The Registrar shall thereupon file the complaint before the appropriate Magistrate under sub-section (1) of Section 81-A of the Act, along with all relevant records, and shall report compliance to the Inspector General of Registration. Provided that penal action shall not be initiated where the part extent of a particular survey number or clearly unidentifiable properties are furnished by the competent authorities and entered by the registering officer in the prohibited property register. (viii) No prosecution shall be instituted against the registering officer under this rule without the prior sanction of the Inspector General of Registration. 188-B. (i) All complaints, notices, reports and orders under Rules 188-A and 188-B shall be recorded in a separate register maintained in Form-2 of the Appendix-XIII. (ii) The Inspector General of Registration may issue guidelines or circulars from time to time for the uniform implementation of Sections 81 -A and 81 -B of the Act, including checklists for verification to establish good faith or due diligence.

items.text: The alleged contraventions are stated to constitute violations of the provisions of the Registration Act, 1908, particularly under Sections 22A, 22B, or 22C, and may attract action under Section 81 -A of the Act. Copies of the documents, records, and other material evidence forming the basis of the allegation are enclosed herewith for your reference. You are hereby called upon to show cause in writing within fifteen (15) days from the date of receipt of this notice as to why disciplinary or other action under Section 81- A of the Registration Act, 1908, should not be initiated against you. Your reply must specifically address each point of allegation and may include supporting documents. If so desired, a personal hearing will be granted, and you may indicate your request for such a hearing in your written reply, specifying convenient dates. Please note that failure to submit your reply within the stipulate d period may result in an ex parte decision being taken against you under Section 81-A of the Act without further notice. This notice is issued under the authority of the [Designated Authority / District Registrar), in exercise of powers conferred under Se ctions 77A and 81 -A of the Registration Act, 1908, and in accordance with the Andhra Pradesh Registration Rules. You are advised to furnish your explanation strictly within the prescribed time frame. items.text: For the establishment of greenfield cement plant, the company has purchased patta lands to an extent of 1393.21 acres.The President - Projects of RAMCO Cements Limited further informed that, out of 1639.40 acres of the mining lease area, the lands in Sy.Nos.408, 545 of Kalvatla village and in Sy.Nos.152, 155 and 168 of Kotapadu village of Kolimigundla Mandal that belongs to Endowments Department measuring in total Ac.17.71cents, fall within the mining lease area. Accordingly, a request was made for alienation of the said lands of said Ac.17.71 cents of Endowment lands on an exchange basis with an equivalent extent of patta lands owned by RAMCO Cements Limited. 2. After careful examination of the proposal and the recommendation of the Commissioner of Endowments, Government hereby accords permission for the exchange of Endowment lands admea suring Ac.17.71 cents, situated in Kalvatala and Kotapadu Villages of Kolimigundla(M), Nandyal District as they fall within the approved mining lease area of M/s. RAMCO Cements Limited, with an equivalent extent of Ac.17.71 cents of patta lands of RAMCO Ce ments Limited situated at Itikyala Village for mining activities of M/s. RAMCO Cements Limited subject to obtaining prior permission of the Hon’ble High Court of Andhra Pradesh, in view of the interim orders dated :07.06.2005 in W.P.M.P.No.15055/2005 in W.P .No. 11812/2005, and also subject to strict compliance with the procedure prescribed under Section 80 of the A.P.Charitable & Hindu Religious Institutions & Endowments Act, 1987. 5. The Commissioner of Endowments, Andhra Pradesh, Vijayawada shall take further necessary action in the matter and ensure that the alternate lands are free from encumbrances and are capable of being put to beneficial use by the concerned endowment Institutions before effecting the exchange. Hence, the Commission recommends to devolve the recommended amount during the award period (Para 7.15.8 & Table 7.34). Decision of the Government: Not accepted for the annual transfer of Rs.1407 Cr .per annum. (Rs.5628 Cr . for the award period of 4 years i.e. from 2026-27 to 2029-2030). Recommendation No.2 Keeping in view the financial requirements of PRIs, the Commission recommends to distribute the recommended funds in the ratio of 70:15:15 to Gram Panchayats, Mandal PrajaParishads and ZillaPrajaParishads respectively (Para 7.15.11). Decision of the Government: Accepted. Whatever Devolution if ever it happens will be in 70:15:15.

items.text: Decision of the Government: Accepted. Whatever Devolution if ever it happens will be in 70:15:15. (Present distribution ratio is 70:20:10) Recommendation No.3 For intra-distribution among GPs, MPPs and ZPPs, the Commission suggests to distribute 80% of the grants on the basis of population and 20% on area basis (Para 7.15.11). Decision of the Government: Accepted. Present intra distribution is 90:10 Recommendation No.4 The Commission strongly recommends to enhance per capita grant to Rs.25/ -, Rs.50/- and Rs.25/- to GPs, MPPs, and ZPPs respectively. The state government has already accepted to enhance the per capita grant to Rs.25/ -, Rs.50/- and Rs.25/- to GPs, MPPs, and ZPPs respectively as per the recommendation made by the fourth State Finance Commission, but not operationalized. This Commission recommends to implement the enhancement of per capita grant as already accepted by the government. The add itional commitment is estimated to be around Rs.295 crores. This Commission opines that the enhancement of per capita grant will give some relief to PRIs in making provision for supply of basic needs (Para 7.8.1). Decision of the Government: Accepted. -4 - Recommendation No.5 The Gram Panchayats with less than 1000 population do not have adequate resources even to pay the electricity charges. This Commission reiterates the recommendation made by the Fourth State Finance Commission that the gram panchayats wi th less than 1000 population should be supported with electricity charges by the government as per actual as already accepted by the government.

items.text: This Commission reiterates the recommendation made by the Fourth State Finance Commission that the gram panchayats wi th less than 1000 population should be supported with electricity charges by the government as per actual as already accepted by the government. Hence the government may release special grant every year equivalent to actual electricity bill of the minor pa nchayats. There are 1895 minor gram panchayats in the state. The required funds for this purpose is estimated to be around Rs.35 crores per annum(Para 7.8.2). Decision of the Government: Rejected. In view of additional financial commitment of Rs.35 Cr .p. a. Necessary amendments may be incorporated in the Act. Decision of the Government: Rejected. Recommendation No.24 To address the issue of undervaluation of property, the Commission recommends constituting a committee with (1) EO -PR&RD (2) Assistant Engineer, Panchayat Raj Dept. (3) Panchayat Secretary (4) Mandal surveyor and (5) Delegate from registration Department. Once the Committee estimates the value of houses of residents, there will not be any opportunity to change it and house tax collection will be significantly improved (Para 7.5.1.6). Decission of the Government: Accepted. CPR is directed to conduct a pilot study. Recommendation No.25 This Commission also recommend to the government to examine the utility and feasibility of the application of scheme namely Survey of Villages Abadi& Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas (SVAMITVA), a central sector scheme in addressing the issue of undervaluation of houses/ properties in villages. Under this, cadastral mapping is conducted using drones and technological tools to accurately demarcate property boundaries and establish ownership rights and enable s proper calculation and collection of property tax. As per the annual report of MoPR for 2023-24, in Andhra Pradesh drone survey has been completed in 13280 villages and property cards were prepared covering 1073 villages (Para 7.5.1.13m). In addition, allocation in the state budget should be reflected under appropriate minor heads (196/197/198) for ZPs, MPPs and GPs to ensure effective execution of devolved activities. Decision of the Government: CPR is directed to submit proposals to the Government. Recommendation No.52 The non-maintenance of critical financial registers in PRIs hinders accurate record - keeping and verification of financial transactions. The Commission recommends that the State PR Dept. should strictly enforce the maintenance of all eight registers under the MAS, particularly those related to immovable and movable properties, receivables and payables, and demand and collection. The supervisory officers during inspections should ensure that these registers are updated and certified properly (Para 9.1.3). Decision of the Government: Accepted Recommendation No.53 The discrepancies between manually prepared accounts and e -GramSwaraj generated accounts indicate serious issues in panchayat financial management. The Commission recommends the State PR Dept. should (a) integrate e - GramSwaraj with CFMS and Panchayat General Funds (b) implement a robust reconciliation mechanism in all the PRIs to align manual accounts with e -Gram Swaraj records. (c) ensure that all receipts and payments are properly recorded in the e-GramSwaraj (Para 9.1.5). Decision of the Government: Accepted. Recommendation No.54 A central repository of financial data for Panchayats is urgently required to enable effective planning and financial management.

The Commission recommends that the State PR Dept. should create a centralized financial database for PRIs at both the district and state levels, to be managed either by the PR&RD Department or the Director of State Audit. This database should consolidate audited financial data from all Panchayats, making it available for financial planning, resource allocation, and audits (Para 9.1.9). Chief Executive officer ZPP to ensure proper financial management, internal auditing, and accountability (Para 9.1.11). items.text: ORDER: The following notification will be published in the Extra-ordinary issue of the Andhra Pradesh Gazette dated: 05-10-2026. NOTIFICATION In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 3 of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 (Act No.13 of 1994), read with the Andhra Pradesh Gram Panchayats (Declaration of Villages) Rules, 2007, and in view of the orders of the Hon’ble High Court of Andhra Pradesh in W.P.No.2738 of 2020, Government hereby declares Velugubanda, Rajanagaram Mandal, East Godavari District as a Village for the purposes of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994. 2. The earlier proposal for inclusion of Velugubanda, Rajanagaram Mandal in the Rajamahendravaram Municipal Corporation pursuant to G.O.Ms.No.261, Panchayat Raj & Rural Development (E&R) Department, dated 28.01.2020, does not survive for operation consequent upon the orders of the Hon’ble High Court of Andhra Pradesh in W.P.No.2738 of 2020. 3. This notification is issued as a fresh declaration under Section 3(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, without reviving or validating the Government Order which was set aside by the Hon’ble High Court and without prejudice to the orders of the Hon’ble High Court in the aforesaid Writ Petition or any other subsisting judicial orders. (P.T.O) ::2:: 4.
